units.function: Pure tests for normalizing and parsing persisted SSH, built-in sandbox, schema-driven sandbox, generic plugin-backed sandbox and plugin environment-driver configuration.
units.dependencyDirection: Vitest -> environment-config service -> HttpError plus driver/provider schemas and in-memory normalization; no database, Secret resolver, runtime host, plugin process or authorization policy is exercised.
units.keyDataModels: Environment driver discriminant, SSH host/port/user/workspace/host-key and private-key Secret reference, sandbox provider/image/template/timeout/reuse lease and plugin key/driver key/driver config.
units.lifecycle: Accept an environment payload -> discriminate driver/provider -> normalize defaults and primitive types -> persist a canonical config object -> parse the stored object into a typed execution-driver configuration.
units.testAssessment: Focused Vitest passed 11/11. The suite gives concise positive coverage and proves raw SSH private keys and relative remote workspace paths are rejected. It does not cover malformed drivers/providers, hostile or oversized nested objects, unknown-key policy, schema evolution/provider removal, Secret authorization and resolution, serialization/redaction, local-enterprise portability or stable error codes.
units.designRationale: Keep the service-side environment envelope stable while allowing execution providers to add configuration without modifying the central server for every provider.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs portable managed-cloud and customer-local execution-node profiles, with vendor-neutral Connector configuration, strict Secret isolation and upgrade-safe provider extensions.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the discriminated driver envelope and provider-extensible configuration boundary. Require a versioned provider schema, field-level Secret/reference annotations, allowlisted persisted keys, structural size/depth limits, structured validation codes, policy validation per execution node and compatibility fixtures for upgrade/downgrade.
units.responsibilityConflict: An execution location/config is operational context, not authorization. The config must be bound to the exact Work, accountable human, Connector capability, data contract, approval digest and runtime attestation; permissive unknown fields cannot silently expand tools, data access or credential scope.
units.securityFindings: HIGH schema/secret-classification gap: generic provider fields are preserved and a credential-shaped apiKey field is accepted directly, so safety depends on external provider-schema behavior not proved here. MEDIUM canonicalization inconsistency: built-in image trimming differs from generic/schema-driven string preservation. MEDIUM validation gap: no hostile nested input, prototype key, resource bound, unknown driver/provider, Secret authorization, redaction or stable error-code tests.
